targets.authors: Walrave M, Waeterloos C, Ponnet K.
targets.title: Adoption of a contact tracing app for containing COVID-19: a health belief model approach.
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, in this study, we have reported the results of a cross-cultural, cohort-based replication of the original study by Walrave et al [ 20 ].
targets.outcome_quote: Nevertheless, perceived benefits and perceived barriers were confirmed as the main, statistically significant predictors of DCT uptake, consistent with the original study (β=.60, P <.001 and β=−.39; P <.001, respectively). Differently from the original study, self-efficacy was not a significant predictor in the strict statistical sense (β=.12; P =.003).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors confirm benefits and barriers but explicitly contrast the nonsignificant self-efficacy finding with the original; cues to action also differed.

reasoning: A new Czech sample re-tests the Belgian published finding; methods and results identify one original paper.
